compiled_state.description:
## Context
ADR 0100 makes the immutable route registry and parser factories authoritative for command identity, grammar, and committed help. Twenty-one visible pure-intercept routes support `rebar <command> --help` but remain absent from overview help and fail under `rebar help <command>`. The `identity` child parsers disable their own help actions, so `rebar identity create --help` reaches top-level usage and exits with an error.

## Plan
- Make the help-backed predicate exactly `not route.hidden and not route.retired` in `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`, and `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py`. Do not add route metadata.
- Add nonblank parser descriptions to `reconcile.build`, `enrich.build`, `identity.build`, and `certs.build_trusted_env` so route-owned summaries populate overview help.
- Move `_unwrap_usage` and `_collapse_metavars` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` into `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`. Apply usage unwrapping only to intercept routes without explicit parser usage. Apply metavar normalization to intercept option lines before byte normalization. Preserve the explicit multiline `trusted-env` usage.
- Expand the generator census through its public entry point. Do not test the private `_expected` helper. Generate one committed artifact for each newly help-backed route and regenerate `overview.txt`.
- Widen top-level help pre-scan to every live visible route. Keep `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` exactly `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, and `workflow` so nonleading child help reaches the owning parser or handler.
- Enable help on the `identity create`, `identity use`, and `identity key` child parsers. Prove that each child returns child usage and exits successfully.
- Keep the explicit `config validate --help` contract because `config validate` is handler-dispatched and has no populated argparse subparser action.
- Keep parser-introspective nested-family coverage for argparse-backed families. Assert that the derived family set matches runtime ownership, then exercise each child-help path. Keep the 42-subprocess all-route contract in the held-out outer oracle.
- Delete `_render_intercept` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`. Make CLI reference generation consume `subcommand_help(route.name)` for every documented route. Update the two legacy expectations in `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`.
- Correct comments and docstrings that claim intercept routes lack committed help. The affected paths include `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`, `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_workflow_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_central_mount_gate_ad9f.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_registry_cutover_s6.py`, and `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`.
- Update affected expectations in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py` and `tests/interfaces/facades/test_intercept_registry_cutover_s6_heldout.py`.
- Retain `_OVERVIEW_OMIT` as exactly `bridge-fsck` and `bridge-probe`. Retain the test allowlist as exactly `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`.
- Keep `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py` scoped away from pure-intercept parsers because generator normalization permits those parsers to retain the standard library formatter.
- Regenerate package help and the CLI reference through their existing generators. The Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 CI cells must pass the help drift check against the same committed bytes.
- Do not add another router, parser, help source, mechanical writing-policy gate, or change to the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every live visible route outside the documented omit set appears exactly once in overview help.
- [x] `rebar help <command>` succeeds for every canonical pure-intercept route returned by the registry.
- [x] The pure-intercept help contract proves that no command handler executes.
- [x] The pure-intercept help contract proves that no ticket store is mounted or created.
- [x] `rebar help <command>` returns the matching committed artifact bytes.
- [x] Top-level `rebar <command> --help` returns the matching committed artifact bytes.
- [x] Every pure-intercept parser factory supplies a nonblank overview description.
- [x] The committed `trusted-env` usage banner preserves separate `add` and `revoke` lines.
- [x] Each CLI-reference pure-intercept syntax block equals the matching committed artifact.
- [x] A repository-wide semantic and string search reports zero `_render_intercept` references.
- [x] All four help-backed census sites use the live-visible predicate.
- [x] The exact overview exemptions remain `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`.
- [x] Hidden aliases and retired spellings remain absent from overview discovery.
- [x] `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` equals `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, and `workflow`.
- [x] Every parser-introspectable nested family returns child-parser usage for each child.
- [x] `rebar identity create --help`, `rebar identity use --help`, and `rebar identity key --help` return their child usage and exit successfully.
- [x] `rebar config validate --help` reaches `build_validate` and returns validate child help.
- [x] Comments and test docstrings describe committed help ownership accurately.
- [x] The help drift check passes on supported Python versions.
- [x] The CLI-reference drift check passes.
- [x] No competing routing, parser, or help mechanism is introduced.
- [x] No mechanical writing enforcement is introduced.
- [x] The Markdown-only reduced test policy remains unchanged.

## CI gate remediation
- Classify the generated `jira-onboard` artifact and overview entry as compatibility surfaces. ADR 0100 records `jira-onboard` as a compatibility shim with a distinct historical invocation. The approved F12 acceptance criteria require the overview omit set to remain unchanged.
- Register the existing `review_result` schema for `scan-spec`.
- Add JSON schemas for the stable `config` and `sign-review` output contracts.
- Extend the CLI output contract test with offline drivers for `config` and `sign-review`.
- Add a reason-bearing CLI driver exemption map in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py` for `review-code`, `review-plan`, `scan-spec`, and `verify-completion` because they invoke model operations. Wire the map into driver classification, require a nonblank reason for every entry, reject stale entries, and reject overlap with offline drivers. The guard documentation permits explicit exemptions, but the current CLI guard does not implement this facility.
- Correct schema registry comments that depend on intercept routes lacking committed help.
- Document the added schemas in the external output catalog.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Retained compatibility spellings are categorized without removing them from generated help.
- [x] Every newly discovered output advertiser has a registered schema.
- [x] Offline output advertisers are exercised against their registered schemas.
- [x] Every model-backed driver exemption has a nonblank reason.
- [x] The fixture-store contract test does not invoke model-backed output advertisers.
- [x] The three CI regressions reproduce red before remediation and pass afterward.
